# ACE: the African Context Engine

> ACE gives checked, local, citable knowledge for Africa on any phone (USSD, SMS/RCS, voice, WhatsApp and MCP). USSD, SMS and voice are the default, so every phone is reached; WhatsApp and RCS show the sources under every answer for people with a smartphone and data, and RCS adds suggested replies and falls back to SMS. RCS shipped in 2.2.0b3 (26 November 2026), switched on country by country. It covers 34 countries in 32 languages. Release 2.4 preview (2.4.0b1 to 2.4.0b3, 27 November 2026) is live at https://ace.korext.com, with an API and MCP at https://ace.korext.com/mcp. Release 2.3 preview (2.3.0b1, 26 November 2026; 2.3.0b2, 27 November, with no default country) added 24 languages, each offered in the countries that speak it: Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Nigerian Pidgin, isiZulu, isiXhosa, Afrikaans, Sesotho, Setswana, Xitsonga, Shona, Chichewa, Bemba, Kinyarwanda, Kirundi, Luganda, Lingala, Akan, Ewe, Wolof, Dyula, Mooré, Pular and Tigrinya. They join English, Swahili, French, Portuguese, Arabic, Amharic, Afaan Oromo and Somali. ACE reads a message with no marker word by its letters, and tells a person when it does not read their language yet, naming the languages it reads in their country, from character profiles of 49 languages its callers speak but ACE does not, such as Gikuyu, Dholuo and Dagbani. Twelve of the new languages have a voice on the voice line through Gemini TTS. No fluent speaker has reviewed the new languages yet. Six decision services built on dated public data (rain this week, official warnings, nearest health facility, market prices, a pregnancy companion and a crop problem check) cover every country wherever open data exists and name the gap where it does not. Release 2.2.0b3 also added the ACE tokenizer audit, which measures what 59 African language varieties cost against English on nine released tokenizers and scores unreleased tokenizers offline (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24565738). Release 2.2 preview (2.2.0b1 and 2.2.0b2, 25 November 2026) added speech and translation: a language check on real speech text from Google's open WAXAL corpus, a voice line that speaks only languages with a known voice (Amharic and Somali through Gemini TTS), and optional Google Cloud speech and translation providers. Release 2.1 (24 November 2026) added 21 countries and five languages, with replies budgeted for the GSM-7 or UCS-2 alphabet each language needs. The caller's dialling code picks the country, a safety rail answers emergencies with that country's verified numbers before anything else runs, and every answer cites its published source. It runs without an AI model. Code is Apache 2.0; open context packs are CC BY 4.0. Created by Tom Bruno.

## Start here

- [Project page](https://tbrunoh.github.io/ace/): the problems ACE solves, how it works, coverage, V2 and answers to common questions
- Essays by the creator: [AI for Africa has to work on the phone people already own](https://tbrunoh.github.io/writing/ai-for-africa-basic-phones/) and [Africa's farm data is open. The last mile to farmers is the work left to do](https://tbrunoh.github.io/writing/africa-farm-data-last-mile/)
- [README](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/README.md): what ACE does, coverage for all 34 countries and a quickstart
- [Architecture](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): the request flow, modules, retrieval, channel budgets, language models and the MCP server
- [Channels](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/channels.md): setup for USSD, SMS, RCS with SMS fallback, voice and WhatsApp
- [Context packs](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/context-packs.md): how sourced facts are written, reviewed and validated
- [Safety and privacy](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/safety-and-privacy.md): what the code guarantees, what every deployment must do and how to report a safety problem

## V2: design published and previews released, 24 to 26 November 2026

- [Speech and translation](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/speech.md): what exists to hear, speak and translate each of the 32 languages, how ACE uses WAXAL, the WAXAL language results, the voice line rule, who pays for Google Cloud use, why a caller cannot run up the bill, and how to cap it, and the gaps
- [Release 2.1 design](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/v2/release-2.1.md): the 21 new countries, the five new languages, the alphabet each reply travels in, the five data problems ACE designs around, decisions and gaps
- [Languages](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/languages.md): the 32 languages and the countries each is offered in, how ACE guesses a language within the caller's country, how it tells a language it does not speak, how African letters reach the SMS alphabet, how confident each draft is, and how to add a language in one file
- [Tokenizer audit](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/benchmark/tokenizer-audit/README.md): what 59 African language varieties cost against English on nine released tokenizers, on FLORES-200 and on ACE's own text and SMS, with intervals, paired tests and an offline check for unreleased tokenizers
- [Back translation reports](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/reviews/README.md): machine back translations of every string in Portuguese, Arabic, Amharic, Afaan Oromo and Somali, with the rows fluent reviewers should check first
- [Services guide](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/services.md): the six services, their decision rules, coverage and gaps in all 34 countries, and how to call them over the API and MCP
- [Connectors](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/connectors/README.md): the public data sources, licences and refresh schedule behind the services
- [V2 overview](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/v2/README.md): twelve decision services built on public data, a voice line in African languages, signed knowledge and a shared grounding layer
- [Product spec](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/v2/product-spec.md): who V2 serves, the services, journeys, architecture, roadmap, measures and risks
- [Data and model catalog](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/v2/data-catalog.md): every public dataset and model V2 builds on, with access and licence
- [Build plan](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/v2/build-plan.md): epics, contracts and evaluation for building V2 with Google Antigravity

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules every AI coding agent follows in this repository
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): how to add knowledge or code

- [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/ROADMAP.md): the 2.4, 2.3, 2.2, 2.1 and 2.0 previews, including the public product in 2.4.0b1, its ACE icons in 2.4.0b2 and fresh data from the first request in 2.4.0b3, 24 languages in 2.3.0b1, no default country in 2.3.0b2 and RCS in 2.2.0b3, and the four V2 phases
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release
